name: com.seedviews/seedviews
title: SeedViews
description: Draft UGC creator castings from an app link. A person approves and pays before any outreach.

tools.name: cast
tools.description: Start a casting: real creators film the app and post it on their own accounts. With dry_run: true nothing is saved and nobody is contacted; you get who SeedViews will look for, the brief, the opening message (opening_message_preview), the price, the totals and the timeline to show your person. Without dry_run a draft is created and the answer holds pay_url (with an API key, a page that takes the payment with no sign-in): your person must open it to pay before any creator hears about it (creator pay plus 5% is collected up front, anything unused is refunded automatically). Plans: $99 a month up to 30 videos live, $249 up to 100, starting when the first video is live. Before your person pays, tell them what the card is charged later, not only now. Creator pay plus 5% when they pay. The card is kept for the plan: $99 a month, first charged when a video passes the check, then every month until they cancel it in the dashboard. In a month with more than 30 videos live, the plan moves to Growth ($249) and the $150 difference is charged that day. A cancelled plan starts again, and is charged, when a video from a casting still running passes the check. plan.charges in the answer says the same. Without an API key the answer includes casting_token: keep it and pass it to every other tool; it is shown once.

store_url.description: The app's App Store or Google Play link. Ask your person if you do not know it.

price_usd.description: What each creator is paid per video, in US dollars (default 25). One price for everyone; creators take it or pass. A higher price gets more yeses.

looking_for.description: Who to look for. Leave it out to use what SeedViews drafts from the store link.

niche.description: The creators' niche, e.g. 'habit tracking, productivity'. For a language app, the languages learned go here, e.g. 'learning Japanese, manga'.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code of the language the creators post in, which is their audience's language, e.g. 'en'. For a language app this is the language the learners already speak ('en'), not the one they learn.

countries.description: Where the creators should live. Leave it out to use the countries drafted from the store listing; an empty list [] means anywhere. Not a hard filter: each creator's country is shown.

brief.description: What the video should show and say. Leave it out to get a draft written from the store listing.

opening_message.description: The template of SeedViews' first message to each creator; leave it out to use the one drafted from the app and brief (opening_message in the answer). It must start with "Hi [name], [a line about one of their videos]. ", which SeedViews writes per creator, as it does any other [field] you add. Write [pay] where the pay goes: it is filled from the casting (opening_message_preview shows it). No other amount, no link, at most 700 characters, ending with one easy question.

notify_url.description: Optional https address that gets a signed POST when a person has something to do or something changed (a video or payout awaiting approval with its deadline, a creator signed, the casting paid, opened or closed). If an approval is still waiting about 12 hours before its deadline, video.approval_reminder includes video_id and deadline (and payout_id when waiting on payment). The answer holds notify_secret once: keep it to check each delivery's seedviews-signature header.

deadline_days.description: Days a creator has from their yes to their last post (default 14).

dry_run.description: true: save nothing, contact nobody, charge nothing; only show what this casting would cost and do.

tools.name: send_offers
tools.description: Approves the brief and the opening message together, so outreach starts: SeedViews begins messaging real creators and sending them the paid offer. This reaches real people; confirm the brief and opening_message_preview with your person first. Optional brief, looking_for and opening_message are final edits; notify_url can be set here too. invite adds creators your person already works with (an email gets the offer at once). If the casting is not paid yet, nothing happens and the answer says which link your person must open to pay.

casting_id.description: The casting id that cast returned.

casting_token.description: The casting_token that cast returned when it was called without an API key. Not needed with an API key.

brief.description: Final version of the brief, if it changed.

looking_for.description: Who to look for. Leave it out to use what SeedViews drafts from the store link.

It must start with "Hi [name], [a line about one of their videos]. ", which SeedViews writes per creator, as it does any other [field] you add. Write [pay] where the pay goes: it is filled from the casting (opening_message_preview shows it). No other amount, no link, at most 700 characters, ending with one easy question.

invite.description: Creators your person already knows, to add to this casting.

email.description: If given, the offer is emailed to them once the casting is open.

tools.name: check_video
tools.description: Without approve, only reads a video's check and approval state (is the post live on the creator's own account, when it counts as approved). approve: true approves it, which lets the creator be paid from money already collected. approve: false needs reason and sends the video back to the creator. Ask your person before deciding unless they told you not to. A checked video nobody answers within 48 hours counts as approved.

casting_id.description: The casting id that cast returned.

casting_token.description: The casting_token that cast returned when it was called without an API key. Not needed with an API key.

approve.description: true approves the video, false sends it back. Leave out to only read.

reason.description: Required with approve: false: what the creator should change.

tools.name: pay_creator
tools.description: Approves one creator payout. The money comes from what was already collected for the casting; the creator is then paid automatically. This moves money: ask your person first unless they told you not to.

casting_id.description: The casting id that cast returned.

casting_token.description: The casting_token that cast returned when it was called without an API key. Not needed with an API key.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Reads the casting: status, the opening message, each creator and their state (found, contacted, replied, signed, filming, posted, checked, paid, passed) with our first message to them, each video with views and cost per 1,000 views, totals, and needs_person (what a human must do next, if anything). Read only. Results take days, not minutes: check once a day, do not poll. When needs_person names a deadline (a checked video counts as approved 48 hours after its check), act that same day, or set notify_url to be told.

casting_id.description: The casting id that cast returned.

casting_token.description: The casting_token that cast returned when it was called without an API key. Not needed with an API key.

tools.name: get_files
tools.description: Lists the original file of every approved or paid video, with its post link and the ad-rights line (12 months from the post date, final video only). Read only.

casting_id.description: The casting id that cast returned.

casting_token.description: The casting_token that cast returned when it was called without an API key. Not needed with an API key.
